title: Mock 1 · Foundations
blurb: Core definitions, categories and the big regulatory numbers across all 13 chapters.

questions.q: What is the essential characteristic that distinguishes alternative investments from traditional investments?
questions.explanation: The workbook states the essential characteristic of alternative investments is illiquidity, whereas traditional investments are defined by liquidity (nearness to cash).
hints: Wrong: no investment class here offers guaranteed returns.
Correct: alternatives are not readily convertible into cash as they are off-market or complex.
Wrong: listing gives liquidity, a feature of traditional investments.
Wrong: alternatives often do not satisfy the need for regular income.

questions.q: Under the SEBI (AIF) Regulations, an Angel Fund is a sub-category of which category of AIF?
questions.explanation: Angel Fund means a sub-category fund under Category I AIF that raises funds from accredited investors.
hints: Wrong: Category II covers PE and debt funds.
Wrong: Category III covers complex trading and leverage.
Correct: angel funds are a sub-category of Category I.
Wrong: Specified AIF is a separate fourth category.

questions.q: Which of the following funds falls under Category II AIF?
options: A private equity fund with no government incentives
questions.explanation: Category II includes AIFs such as private equity funds or debt funds for which no specific incentives or concessions are given by the government or any other regulator.
hints: Wrong: social impact funds are Category I.
Wrong: SME funds are Category I.
Correct: PE and debt funds without specific incentives are Category II.
Wrong: special situation funds are a Category I sub-category.

questions.q: What is the minimum capital commitment that an AIF may accept from a regular (non-accredited, non-employee) investor?
questions.explanation: Under the AIF Regulations, an AIF shall not accept from an investor a commitment of less than ₹1 crore (₹25 lakh for employees/directors; not applicable to accredited investors).
hints: Wrong: ₹25 lakh applies to employees/directors of the AIF or manager.
Correct: minimum investment of each investor is ₹1 crore.
Wrong: not a threshold in the AIF Regulations.
Wrong: ₹10 crore is the minimum for a Special Situation Fund.

questions.q: What is the minimum tenure of a Category I or Category II AIF scheme?
questions.explanation: Category I and II AIFs are close ended and the tenure is determined at application subject to a minimum tenure of three years.
hints: Correct: minimum tenure of three years.
Wrong: no 5-year minimum exists (5 years is the AI-only extension cap).
Wrong: not prescribed.
Wrong: too short; Category I and II are close-ended long-term funds.

questions.q: Any material alteration to the investment strategy of an AIF requires the consent of:
options: At least 51% of unit holders by number
At least two-thirds of unit holders by value of their investment
At least 75% of unit holders by number
questions.explanation: Any material alteration to the fund strategy shall be made with the consent of at least two-thirds of unit holders by value of their investment in the AIF or scheme.
hints: Wrong: the test is by value, and the threshold is two-thirds.
Correct: two-thirds by value is the threshold for material strategy change.
Wrong: 75% by value applies to other matters such as investing in associates.
Wrong: investor consent is mandatory.

questions.q: Each scheme of an AIF must have a minimum corpus of:
questions.explanation: Regulation 10(b): each scheme of the AIF shall have a corpus of at least twenty crore rupees.
hints: Wrong: not the prescribed minimum.
Correct: each scheme shall have a corpus of at least ₹20 crore.
Wrong: not the prescribed minimum.
Wrong: ₹100 crore is the minimum corpus for a Special Situation Fund scheme.

questions.q: Which legal structure is most commonly used to set up a domestic AIF in India?
questions.explanation: Almost all AIFs formed in India follow the trust structure because of operational advantages, lower compliance cost and a favourable regulatory framework.
hints: Wrong: the company form is least preferred as it is not tax neutral.
Wrong: LLPs are popular abroad but need higher compliance in India.
Wrong: an NBFC is not an AIF structure.
Correct: almost all Indian AIFs are trusts due to operational, cost and tax advantages.

questions.q: For AIF purposes, which kind of trust is considered most appropriate?
questions.explanation: For AIF purposes an 'irrevocably settled, determinate trust' is considered more appropriate, which is why the corpus is divided into units.
hints: Correct: each beneficiary's share must be distinctly ascertainable and the corpus irrevocably vested.
Wrong: in an indeterminate trust shares are not demarcated.
Wrong: public trusts serve charitable purposes.
Wrong: family trusts are excluded from the AIF definition.

questions.q: TVPI of a fund is equal to:
questions.explanation: TVPI can be calculated as (cumulative distributions + residual value) ÷ PIC, or by adding DPI and RVPI.
hints: Wrong: values are added, not subtracted.
Wrong: PIC multiple measures how invested the fund is.
Wrong: this ratio has no meaning as a performance metric.
Correct: total value multiple = realised (DPI) + unrealised (RVPI).

questions.q: A fund has commitments of ₹500 crore, of which investors have paid in ₹400 crore. What is its PIC multiple?
questions.explanation: PIC multiple = paid-in capital ÷ capital commitments = 400 ÷ 500 = 0.80, meaning 80% of commitments have been drawn.
hints: Wrong: this is commitments ÷ paid-in, the inverse.
Wrong: 0.20 is the undrawn share.
Wrong: arithmetic error.

questions.q: Which of the following is the most important investor risk that leads SEBI to require Category I and II AIFs to be close-ended?
questions.explanation: Under the AIF Regulations, Category I and II AIFs need to be close ended because such investments are primarily illiquid.
hints: Correct: Category I and II investments are primarily illiquid, hence close-ended.
Wrong: not related to AIF structure.
Wrong: most Cat I/II holdings are unlisted.
Wrong: applies to derivatives trading, not Cat I/II funds.

questions.q: A term sheet executed between an AIF and a potential investee company is:
options: The private placement memorandum of the fund
A non-binding document with a validity period
A document filed with SEBI for approval
questions.explanation: A term sheet (LOI/SOPT) is a non-binding document that provides no contractual rights; it has a validity period within which the parties are expected to complete the transaction.
hints: Wrong: the SSA is a binding definitive agreement signed later.
Wrong: the PPM is the fund's offer document to investors.
Correct: the term sheet is non-binding and has a validity period.
Wrong: term sheets are not filed with SEBI.

questions.q: A right that obliges promoters to sell their shares to the same buyer on the same terms when the AIF decides to exit is called:
questions.explanation: A drag-along right creates an obligation on other shareholders to sell to the purchaser if the holder of the right chooses to sell; used when the AIF is a minority investor.
hints: Wrong: tag-along lets the holder join a sale initiated by another shareholder.
Correct: drag-along drags other shareholders into the sale.
Wrong: ROFR gives first chance to buy shares being sold.
Wrong: pre-emption protects percentage holding in new issues.

questions.q: According to the workbook, the three factors fundamental to fund selection by an investor are:
options: Credit rating, listing status, dividend history
Brand of distributor, size of commission, location of fund office
Lock-in period, NAV frequency, exit load
Ownership structure and continuing interest, alignment of interests, competing or outside interests
questions.explanation: At the highest level, three factors are fundamental in fund selection: (a) ownership structure and continuing interest, (b) alignment of interests and (c) competing or outside interests.
hints: Wrong: these relate to listed securities.
Wrong: these are not fund-quality factors and hint at conflicts.
Wrong: these are mutual-fund style features.
Correct: these are the three highest-level factors listed in section 8.2.

questions.q: A 'key man clause' in an AIF's fund documents typically:
options: Guarantees a minimum return to investors
Allows investors to redeem units on demand
Prohibits new investments if key persons are not available to devote the necessary time
Fixes the salary of the key investment team
questions.explanation: A key man clause prohibits the AIF/management company from making new investments if one or more key persons are not available to devote the necessary time.
hints: Wrong: AIFs cannot guarantee returns.
Wrong: Category I and II AIFs are close-ended.
Correct: it protects investors who relied on specific key persons.
Wrong: remuneration is not the purpose of this clause.

questions.q: Under SEBI's performance benchmarking framework, benchmarking of AIF performance is carried out:
options: Quarterly, based on data at each quarter end
Only once, at the end of the fund's tenure
Half-yearly, based on data as on September 30 and March 31
questions.explanation: Performance benchmarking shall be done on a half yearly basis based on the data as on September 30 and March 31 of each year.
hints: Wrong: quarterly reports go to SEBI, but benchmarking is half-yearly.
Wrong: AIFs do not have monthly NAV benchmarking.
Wrong: benchmarking is periodic, not one-time.
Correct: half-yearly as of 30 September and 31 March.

questions.q: Which of the following is the BEST first step for an AIF distributor before recommending any scheme?
options: Recommend the scheme that pays the highest commission
Recommend the scheme with the largest corpus
Build a customer-specific risk profile from the investor's objectives, tenure, risk appetite and liquidity needs
Share the side letters signed by other investors
questions.explanation: As a first step, the distributor should have detailed discussions with the prospective investor to formulate a customer-specific risk profile (objectives, tenure, risk appetite, return expectations, liquidity).
hints: Wrong: commission-driven selling is a malpractice.
Wrong: size alone does not establish suitability.
Correct: the workbook says the first step is detailed discussion to formulate a unique risk profile.
Wrong: side letters are confidential and bilateral.

questions.q: The Investment Management Agreement of an AIF set up as a trust is entered into between:
options: The trustee (on behalf of the AIF) and the investment manager
questions.explanation: The IMA is required to be entered into between the trustee (on behalf of the AIF) and the investment manager; the trustee delegates its investment management powers.
hints: Correct: the trustee delegates investment management powers to the manager through the IMA.
Wrong: the custodian agreement is separate.
Wrong: SEBI is not a party to fund contracts.
Wrong: that relationship is not governed by the IMA.

questions.q: A clause that prevents any other investor from receiving more favourable terms than a particular investor is called:
questions.explanation: An investor may insist on a 'Most Favoured Nation' clause to prevent any other investor being placed in a better position than itself.
hints: Correct: MFN protects against better terms being given to others.
Wrong: key man relates to availability of key persons.
Wrong: clawback recovers excess carry from the manager.
Wrong: drag-along is an exit right at investee level.

questions.q: Under the AIF Regulations, an AIF must provide reports to investors at least annually within how many days from the year end?
questions.explanation: Regulation 22: AIF shall provide at least on an annual basis, within 180 days from the year end, reports to investors including financial information of investee companies and material risks.
hints: Wrong: not the prescribed period.
Wrong: 30 days applies to the Annual Activity Report to SEBI.
Wrong: far beyond the prescribed limit.
Correct: at least annually, within 180 days from the year end.

questions.q: Category I and Category II AIFs must value their investments at least once in every:
questions.explanation: Category I and II AIFs shall undertake valuation at least once in every six months by an independent valuer; this may be enhanced to one year with 75% investor approval.
hints: Correct: at least once every six months by an independent valuer.
Wrong: no quarterly mandate.
Wrong: one year is allowed only with approval of 75% of investors by value.
Wrong: too infrequent.

questions.q: Under the Income Tax Act, which income of a Category I or II AIF ('Investment Fund') is taxed at the fund level?
questions.explanation: Income other than business income is exempt at fund level and taxed in investors' hands; business income is taxable at fund level (MMR for trusts).
hints: Wrong: capital gains pass through to investors.
Wrong: dividends pass through to investors.
Correct: business income is taxed at fund level and exempt for investors.
Wrong: interest passes through to investors.

questions.q: Which of the following is a prohibited practice for an AIF distributor?
options: Encouraging investors to read the PPM
Disclosing the hurdle rate and fees to investors
Sharing part of the distribution commission with the investor (pass-back)
questions.explanation: Distributors should not extend pass-backs (giving back part of commission to investors) as this is an inherent conflict; they shall not rebate commissions to investors.
hints: Wrong: this is a good practice.
Wrong: full disclosure is a good practice.
Wrong: IPV by own staff is a good practice.
Correct: pass-backs are an unfair practice and create conflict.

questions.q: The four pillars of AIF distributorship identified in the workbook are:
options: Marketing, sales, support and relationship management
Underwriting, listing, market making and clearing
questions.explanation: Marketing, sales, support and relationship management form the four pillars of AIF distributorship, supported by research and product analysis.
hints: Correct: these form the four pillars of AIF distributorship.
Wrong: these are broking/custody functions.
Wrong: these are merchant banking/exchange functions.
Wrong: these are fund administration functions.
